s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty with mastication
Numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the skin
Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum
Macroglossia, glossitis, and a hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement leading to difficulty with mastication
3-month history of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma complicated by anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Patient is taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements
Platelet count is within normal range
Prothrombin time is slightly elevated
Activated partial thromboplastin time is elevated
Serum zinc level is low
Biopsy from left groin showed subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining
Direct immunofluorescence test was negative
Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab was negative

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive painful blisters and ulcers with systemic symptoms and history of multiple myeloma

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of multiple myeloma and presence of apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and presence of painful blisters and ulcers

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and presence of painful blisters and ulcers

shortlist.label: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and presence of painful blisters and ulcers

shortlist.label: Zinc deficiency disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Low serum zinc level and presence of skin lesions and ulcers

shortlist.label: Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining and history of multiple myeloma

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma-associated neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of multiple myeloma and presence of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs

raw.rationale: The patient's history of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and the presence of apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining in the biopsy are indicative of amyloidosis, which is a known complication of multiple myeloma. The patient's symptoms, including painful blisters and ulcers, macroglossia, and numbness without weakness, can be explained by amyloid deposition in various tissues.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: Negative direct immunofluorescence test and lack of specific autoantibodies make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate but negative direct immunofluorescence test does not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not specifically support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis
rejected.why: Negative direct immunofluorescence test and lack of linear IgA deposits make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Zinc deficiency disorder
rejected.why: While the patient has a low serum zinc level, the clinical presentation and biopsy findings suggest a more complex underlying condition

rejected.label: Amyloidosis
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis, but the specific association with multiple myeloma makes the latter a more precise diagnosis

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma-associated neuropathy
rejected.why: While the patient has numbness without weakness, the presence of systemic symptoms and biopsy findings suggest a more widespread condition like amyloidosis
